_meta.purpose: Compiler fingerprint catalog used by the re-rizin list_functions_with_metadata tool to attach a 'compiled_by' hint to each function. The hints are observed patterns (RSDS debug signature, .CRT section prefix, mangled-name scheme) — no product names.

compiler_categories.msvc: Functions compiled with Microsoft's MSVC toolchain. The .CRT section prefix is .CRT$XC; mangled names start with ?@; debug info is the standard PDB CodeView.
compiler_categories.gcc: Functions compiled with the GNU Compiler Collection. The .CRT section prefix is .init_array; mangled names use the Itanium ABI (_Z); debug info is DWARF.
compiler_categories.clang: Functions compiled with Clang/LLVM. The .CRT section prefix is .init_array; mangled names use the Itanium ABI; debug info is DWARF. Distinguishing from GCC requires the build-id or the presence of Clang's __cxxabiv1 namespace imports.
compiler_categories.icc: Functions compiled with Intel's ICC. Distinguishing from MSVC requires the Intel-specific .CRT section (.CRT$XC with __intel_* symbols).
compiler_categories.rustc: Functions compiled with rustc. The mangled names start with _ZN; the .CRT section is .init_array; the function name pattern is hash-suffixed (a Rust symbol like '_ZN3std2io5Write9write_all17h8c2a3b1e9d4a5b6E' is rustc-stable).
compiler_categories.go: Functions compiled with the Go toolchain. The mangled names contain '..func' or '..stkobj' separators; the .gopclntab section is unique to Go.
compiler_categories.delphi: Functions compiled with Embarcadero Delphi. The mangled names contain '@<unit>@<symbol>$qqrv' or similar patterns; the .itext / .data section prefix is Delphi-specific.

evidence_legend.section_prefix: The .CRT / .init section name prefix is the canonical signal.
evidence_legend.mangled_prefix: The first 3 characters of the demangled name is the canonical signal.
evidence_legend.debug_format: The presence of CodeView (RSDS) vs DWARF debug info is a signal.

fingerprints.note: Canonical MSVC .CRT section. The '$' + single uppercase letter is the MSVC convention for ordered init sections.
MSVC mangled-name scheme. Functions exported from a .dll start with '?@'; C++ type info starts with '??'.
Canonical GCC .init_array / .fini_array. Shared with Clang; distinguishing requires the .debug_info build-id.
Itanium C++ ABI mangled-name scheme. Shared with Clang and rustc; distinguishing requires the hash-suffix style.
Clang's libcxxabi import marker. Distinguishes Clang from GCC when the .init_array section is ambiguous.
ICC's .CRT section contains __intel_* initialization symbols. Distinguishes ICC from MSVC.
rustc stable mangled-name scheme. The 16-character hex suffix is a TypeName hash that rustc uses to dedup symbol names. Distinguishes rustc from C++ Clang/GCC.
Go's program-counter-line-number table. Unique to Go binaries; presence confirms a Go target.
Go's symbol-naming scheme uses '..' as a category separator. The '..func' separator is the most common in a Go binary.
Delphi's mangled-name scheme. The '@UnitName@MethodName$qqrv' pattern is the canonical signal. Pairs with the .itext / .data section prefix.
Delphi's standard section set. The 'itext' section is the canonical signal — no other compiler uses it.
